Liquid crystals

Liquid crystals are made of elongated molecules, which keep a common orientation (the director) while flowing like a liquid. Here, the molecule is 5CB (4-cyano-4'-pentylbiphenyl), the classic room-temperature nematic liquid crystal, packed in two arrangements: a nematic phase, with the molecules aligned along z, and a cholesteric (twisted) phase, with the director turning in the xy plane from one layer to the next, along a helix. The orientations are set by the rotation constraint, constrain_rotation, which keeps the angle between an axis and a vector of the molecule within a range.

Files: 5cb.pdb, and the input files nematic.inp and cholesteric.inp.

The molecule

5cb.pdb is 5CB with its pentyl chain in the extended (all-trans) conformation (built from its SMILES string, CCCCCc1ccc(cc1)-c1ccc(cc1)C#N, with Open Babel, and minimized with the MMFF94 force field). Atom 1 is the end of the alkyl chain, and atom 19 the nitrogen of the cyano group: the vector from atom 1 to atom 19, 15.8 Å long, is the long axis of the molecule, and it is the vector given to constrain_rotation, in its atoms (from) and to lines.

The molecules of a nematic phase are aligned along the director, but as many point one way as the other: the phase is apolar. So each arrangement has two structure blocks, one with the vector of the molecules along the director, and one with it opposite.

The numbers of molecules

The density of 5CB is 1.02 g/mL near room temperature, and its molar mass 249.35 g/mol: 0.00246 molecules per Å³. The nematic phase fills a periodic cube of 50 Å (125000 Å³) with 308 molecules, 154 in each direction. Each layer of the cholesteric phase is 50 × 50 × 15 Å (37500 Å³), with 92 molecules, 46 in each direction.

Nematic phase

Command line

#
# Nematic phase of 5CB (4-cyano-4'-pentylbiphenyl): the molecules aligned along z,
# half of them pointing up and half down, in a periodic cubic box
#
tolerance 2.0
output nematic.pdb

# Uncomment to write only the initial placement of the molecules to the output file,
# without packing them (to check the constraints):
# check_initial_placement

# Periodic box of 50 Å, centered at the origin: 308 molecules of 5CB, 1.02 g/mL
pbc -25. -25. -25. 25. 25. 25.

# The vector from the end of the alkyl chain (atom 1) to the nitrogen of the cyano
# group (atom 19) within 20° of +z
structure 5cb.pdb
  number 154
  constrain_rotation z 0. 20.
    atoms 1
    to 19
  end constrain_rotation
end structure

# ... and within 20° of -z
structure 5cb.pdb
  number 154
  constrain_rotation z 180. 20.
    atoms 1
    to 19
  end constrain_rotation
end structure

constrain_rotation z 0. 20. keeps the vector from atom 1 to atom 19 within 20° of +z, and constrain_rotation z 180. 20. within 20° of -z. Run it with:

packmol nematic.inp

It packs in a few seconds. The cone of 20° sets the order of the phase: the nematic order parameter, $S = \langle 3\cos^2\theta - 1 \rangle / 2$ ($\theta$ the angle of a molecule with the director), is 0.89 in the packed system, while 5CB has about 0.6 near room temperature: a cone of 45° gives 0.59.

Julia

using Packmol, PDBTools# The vector from atom 1 (end of the chain) to atom 19 (cyano N) within 20° of +z and -zup = structure_type("5cb.pdb"; number = 154,    constrain_rotation = Dict(:z => (0.0, 20.0, [1], [19])),)down = structure_type("5cb.pdb"; number = 154,    constrain_rotation = Dict(:z => (180.0, 20.0, [1], [19])),)nematic = PackmolSystem([up, down];    output = "nematic.pdb",    tolerance = 2.0,    unitcell = [50. 0. 0.; 0. 50. 0.; 0. 0. 50.], # centered at the origin    # check_initial_placement = true,)packmol(nematic)nematic.status
:packing_ready

The packed system, with the visualize function of PDBTools.jl (drag to rotate, scroll to zoom), the molecules pointing up in red and those pointing down in blue:

visualize(get_atoms(nematic),    "chain A" => (style = :sticks, color = "red"),    "chain B" => (style = :sticks, color = "blue");    unitcell = UnitCell(nematic.unitcell),    unitcell_origin = -sum(eachcol(nematic.unitcell)) / 2,)

Cholesteric phase

In a cholesteric (chiral nematic) phase, the director turns along a helix: the molecules of each layer lie in the xy plane, aligned along a director that turns from one layer to the next. 5CB forms it when a chiral molecule is added to it; in a twisted nematic cell, the arrangement of a pixel of a liquid crystal display, the twist is instead imposed by the walls of the cell. Here, the cell has four layers of 15 Å, with the director at 0°, 45°, 90° and 135° from x: the next layer, through the periodic boundary along z, would be at 180°, the same as 0° for an apolar director, so the twist continues through the boundary, along a helix of a pitch of 120 Å (a full turn of the director).

The direction of a molecule in a plane takes more than one angle: at 45° from x, the vector is also at 45° from y (at -45° from x, it would be at 135° from y), and at 90° from z. So each structure block has three rotation constraints, one for each axis: for a vector at an angle φ from x in the plane, (cos φ, sin φ, 0), its angles are acos(cos φ) with x, acos(sin φ) with y, and 90° with z. The molecules pointing the other way are at φ + 180°.

Command line

The input file cholesteric.inp (click to expand)
#
# Cholesteric (twisted) phase of 5CB (4-cyano-4'-pentylbiphenyl): four layers of
# molecules lying in the xy plane, with the director turning by 45° from one layer to
# the next. The twist continues through the periodic boundary along z (the director at
# 180° is the one at 0°): a helix with a pitch of 120 Å.
#
tolerance 2.0
output cholesteric.pdb

# Uncomment to write only the initial placement of the molecules to the output file,
# without packing them (to check the constraints):
# check_initial_placement

# Periodic box of 50 x 50 x 60 Å, centered at the origin: layers of 15 Å from
# z = -30 to 30 Å, 92 molecules each (1.02 g/mL)
pbc -25. -25. -30. 25. 25. 30.

# Layer 1, from z = -30 to -15 Å: the director at 0° from x, in the xy plane. The
# vector from the end of the chain (atom 1) to the cyano nitrogen (atom 19) of half of
# the molecules at 0° from x in the plane, and of the other half at 180°
# (antiparallel): its angles with x and y are those of (cos φ, sin φ, 0)
structure 5cb.pdb
  number 46
  above plane 0. 0. 1. -30.
  below plane 0. 0. 1. -15.
  constrain_rotation x 0.0 15.
    atoms 1
    to 19
  end constrain_rotation
  constrain_rotation y 90.0 15.
    atoms 1
    to 19
  end constrain_rotation
  constrain_rotation z 90. 10.
    atoms 1
    to 19
  end constrain_rotation
end structure
structure 5cb.pdb
  number 46
  above plane 0. 0. 1. -30.
  below plane 0. 0. 1. -15.
  constrain_rotation x 180.0 15.
    atoms 1
    to 19
  end constrain_rotation
  constrain_rotation y 90.0 15.
    atoms 1
    to 19
  end constrain_rotation
  constrain_rotation z 90. 10.
    atoms 1
    to 19
  end constrain_rotation
end structure

# Layer 2, from z = -15 to 0 Å: the director at 45° from x, in the xy plane. The
# vector from the end of the chain (atom 1) to the cyano nitrogen (atom 19) of half of
# the molecules at 45° from x in the plane, and of the other half at 225°
# (antiparallel): its angles with x and y are those of (cos φ, sin φ, 0)
structure 5cb.pdb
  number 46
  above plane 0. 0. 1. -15.
  below plane 0. 0. 1. 0.
  constrain_rotation x 45.0 15.
    atoms 1
    to 19
  end constrain_rotation
  constrain_rotation y 45.0 15.
    atoms 1
    to 19
  end constrain_rotation
  constrain_rotation z 90. 10.
    atoms 1
    to 19
  end constrain_rotation
end structure
structure 5cb.pdb
  number 46
  above plane 0. 0. 1. -15.
  below plane 0. 0. 1. 0.
  constrain_rotation x 135.0 15.
    atoms 1
    to 19
  end constrain_rotation
  constrain_rotation y 135.0 15.
    atoms 1
    to 19
  end constrain_rotation
  constrain_rotation z 90. 10.
    atoms 1
    to 19
  end constrain_rotation
end structure

# Layer 3, from z = 0 to 15 Å: the director at 90° from x, in the xy plane. The
# vector from the end of the chain (atom 1) to the cyano nitrogen (atom 19) of half of
# the molecules at 90° from x in the plane, and of the other half at 270°
# (antiparallel): its angles with x and y are those of (cos φ, sin φ, 0)
structure 5cb.pdb
  number 46
  above plane 0. 0. 1. 0.
  below plane 0. 0. 1. 15.
  constrain_rotation x 90.0 15.
    atoms 1
    to 19
  end constrain_rotation
  constrain_rotation y 0.0 15.
    atoms 1
    to 19
  end constrain_rotation
  constrain_rotation z 90. 10.
    atoms 1
    to 19
  end constrain_rotation
end structure
structure 5cb.pdb
  number 46
  above plane 0. 0. 1. 0.
  below plane 0. 0. 1. 15.
  constrain_rotation x 90.0 15.
    atoms 1
    to 19
  end constrain_rotation
  constrain_rotation y 180.0 15.
    atoms 1
    to 19
  end constrain_rotation
  constrain_rotation z 90. 10.
    atoms 1
    to 19
  end constrain_rotation
end structure

# Layer 4, from z = 15 to 30 Å: the director at 135° from x, in the xy plane. The
# vector from the end of the chain (atom 1) to the cyano nitrogen (atom 19) of half of
# the molecules at 135° from x in the plane, and of the other half at 315°
# (antiparallel): its angles with x and y are those of (cos φ, sin φ, 0)
structure 5cb.pdb
  number 46
  above plane 0. 0. 1. 15.
  below plane 0. 0. 1. 30.
  constrain_rotation x 135.0 15.
    atoms 1
    to 19
  end constrain_rotation
  constrain_rotation y 45.0 15.
    atoms 1
    to 19
  end constrain_rotation
  constrain_rotation z 90. 10.
    atoms 1
    to 19
  end constrain_rotation
end structure
structure 5cb.pdb
  number 46
  above plane 0. 0. 1. 15.
  below plane 0. 0. 1. 30.
  constrain_rotation x 45.0 15.
    atoms 1
    to 19
  end constrain_rotation
  constrain_rotation y 135.0 15.
    atoms 1
    to 19
  end constrain_rotation
  constrain_rotation z 90. 10.
    atoms 1
    to 19
  end constrain_rotation

packmol cholesteric.inp

It packs in about a second with 14 threads.

Julia

The same input, with the structure types of the layers built in a loop:

# The vector from atom 1 to atom 19 at the angle φ from x, in the xy plane: within 15°# of its angles with x and y, and 10° of the planefunction layer(z1, z2, φ)    return structure_type("5cb.pdb"; number = 46,        constraints = [AbovePlane([0., 0., 1.], z1), BelowPlane([0., 0., 1.], z2)],        constrain_rotation = Dict(            :x => (acosd(cosd(φ)), 15.0, [1], [19]),            :y => (acosd(sind(φ)), 15.0, [1], [19]),            :z => (90.0, 10.0, [1], [19]),        ),    )endstructure_types = Packmol.StructureType{3,Float64}[]for (k, φ) in enumerate((0.0, 45.0, 90.0, 135.0))    z1 = -30.0 + 15 * (k - 1)    push!(structure_types, layer(z1, z1 + 15, φ))    push!(structure_types, layer(z1, z1 + 15, φ + 180)) # antiparallelendcholesteric = PackmolSystem(structure_types;    output = "cholesteric.pdb",    tolerance = 2.0,    unitcell = [50. 0. 0.; 0. 50. 0.; 0. 0. 60.], # centered at the origin)packmol(cholesteric)cholesteric.status
:packing_ready

The layers, from the bottom to the top, in red, orange, green and blue (each structure type is written with a chain identifier of its own, from A to H): seen from above, the director turns by 45° from one layer to the next.

visualize(get_atoms(cholesteric),    "chain A or chain B" => (style = :sticks, color = "red"),    "chain C or chain D" => (style = :sticks, color = "orange"),    "chain E or chain F" => (style = :sticks, color = "green"),    "chain G or chain H" => (style = :sticks, color = "blue");    unitcell = UnitCell(cholesteric.unitcell),    unitcell_origin = -sum(eachcol(cholesteric.unitcell)) / 2,)

get_atoms(packmol_system::PackmolSystem)

Returns the atoms of the packed system, with their current coordinates.

PackmolSystem(structure_types::Vector{<:StructureType}; output::String, kwargs...)

Build a PackmolSystem directly from a vector of StructureTypes (see structure_type), without going through an input file.

packmol(input_file::String; options...) packmol(packmol_system::PackmolSystem; options...) packmol( system::SolutionBoxUS; output="system.pdb", # box size box_sides::AbstractVector{<:Number}, # or margin::Number, pbc::Symbol = :cubic, kwargs..., ) packmol( system::SolutionBoxUSC; concentration::Number, concentration_units::Union{Nothing,String} = nothing, output="system.pdb", # box size box_sides::AbstractVector{<:Number}, # or margin::Number, pbc::Symbol = :cubic, kwargs..., ) packmol( system::SolutionBoxUWI; ionic_concentration::Number=0.15u"mol/L", output="system.pdb", # box size box_sides::AbstractVector{<:Number}, # or margin::Number, pbc::Symbol = :cubic, kwargs..., ) packmol( system::Membrane; output="membrane.pdb", kwargs..., ) packmol(system::MembraneProtein; output = "membrane_protein.pdb", kwargs...)

Read a Packmol input file, run the packing optimization, and write the output.

structure_type(filename; number, constraints=Constraint[], tolerance=2.0, radius=nothing, fixed=nothing, center=:none, residue_numbering=-1, D=3, T=Float64)

Build a StructureType for number copies of the molecule read from the PDB file filename, without going through an input file.

packmol(system::MembraneProtein; output = "membrane_protein.pdb", kwargs...)

Builds and packs a membrane protein system, without writing an input file (as write_packmol_input followed by packmol).

packmol( system::Membrane; output="membrane.pdb", kwargs..., )

Builds and packs a lipid membrane system, without writing an input file.

packmol( system::SolutionBoxUSC; concentration::Number, concentration_units::Union{Nothing,String} = nothing, output="system.pdb", # box size box_sides::AbstractVector{<:Number}, # or margin::Number, pbc::Symbol = :cubic, kwargs..., )

Builds and packs a Solute + Solvent + Cossolvent system, without writing an input file.

packmol( system::SolutionBoxUS; output="system.pdb", # box size box_sides::AbstractVector{<:Number}, # or margin::Number, pbc::Symbol = :cubic, kwargs..., )

Builds and packs a Solute + Solvent system, without writing an input file.

packmol( system::SolutionBoxUWI; ionic_concentration::Number=0.15u"mol/L", output="system.pdb", # box size box_sides::AbstractVector{<:Number}, # or margin::Number, pbc::Symbol = :cubic, kwargs..., )

Builds and packs a Solute + Water + Ions system, without writing an input file.
